turns.answer:
Absolutely! A NAS can host a Minecraft server for you and your friends 24/7, even when your gaming PC is turned off.

In fact, a NAS can be a pretty good Minecraft host because it:

Runs continuously with relatively low power consumption.

Can host Minecraft in Docker containers.

Lets friends connect remotely over the internet.

Can run backups automatically.

Can host other services alongside Minecraft, such as Plex, Jellyfin, or file sharing.

However, not every NAS is powerful enough. Minecraft benefits much more from CPU performance and RAM than from storage capacity.

My recommendations

For a Minecraft server, I'd prioritize these features:

Intel or AMD CPU with strong single-core performance.

At least 16 GB RAM, preferably upgradeable.

Docker or container support.

SSD storage for the Minecraft world.

1GbE or faster networking.

How to set it up

I'd use Docker + itzg's Minecraft Server container.

The basic setup:

Install Docker or the NAS's container management application.

Download the itzg/minecraft-server image.

Allocate 4–6 GB RAM to the server.

Mount an SSD-backed folder for world data.

Configure Java version, game version, and server type (Vanilla, Paper, Fabric, or Forge).

Forward TCP port 25565 on your router.

Enable a whitelist so only your friends can join.

Keep the NAS administration interface private. Only expose the game server port, and configure automatic world backups.
